=You are a senior QA engineer. Analyze the following JIRA user story and its existing test cases, then perform two tasks.

## JIRA Story
Story ID: {{$json.story_id}}
Summary: {{$json.summary}}

Description:
{{$json.description}}

Acceptance Criteria:
{{$json.acceptance_criteria}}

## Existing Test Cases ({{$json.linked_testcases.length}} linked)
{{JSON.stringify($json.linked_testcases, null, 2)}}

---

## TASK 1 — Coverage Summary
Summarize what is already covered by the existing test cases. Structure it as:
- Functional scenarios covered
- Edge cases covered
- Validation checks covered
- Negative scenarios covered

## TASK 2 — Missing Scenarios
Identify ALL testing gaps. Consider:
- Boundary conditions not tested
- Negative / error paths not covered
- Validation rules not verified
- Error handling scenarios
- Integration / end-to-end flows
- Any acceptance criteria not covered by existing tests

Return your analysis as valid JSON only (no markdown fences, no extra text) in this exact structure:
{
  "coverage_summary": {
    "functional_scenarios": ["..."],
    "edge_cases": ["..."],
    "validation_checks": ["..."],
    "negative_scenarios": ["..."]
  },
  "missing_scenarios": [
    {
      "title": "short title",
      "description": "what needs to be tested and why it is missing",
      "category": "boundary|negative|validation|error_handling|integration|functional"
    }
  ]
}

=Format the following QA Test Design Agent results as a clear, human-readable summary for a QA engineer.

Data:
{{JSON.stringify($json, null, 2)}}

Format as:
1. Story overview (ID + summary)
2. Existing test coverage summary (bullet points per category)
3. Missing scenarios identified (numbered list with categories)
4. New test cases created (list with keys and names)
5. Overall assessment (1-2 sentences)

Use clear headings. Be concise but complete.
